races.name: Available Car Selling Stakes

runners_data.name: Beach Ahead
runners_data.note: Lightly raced two-year-old with only two runs and a modest best of fourth, showing minimal progression; going and trip are fine but the unknown style and lack of a win or place frame make it a difficult proposition here.
runners_data.comment: Twice fourth in his last two starts, this colt was dropped in grade on softer ground when beaten three and a half lengths in a seller at Goodwood latest, and stepping back to six furlongs, where he's shown his form, should suit; our rating has him firmly in the mix, though a big weight and first-time tongue-tie leave a couple of questions.

runners_data.name: Champagne Charlee
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams two-year-old with no recorded form or going profile, making any assessment speculative; the stable's Leicester record warrants a token mention but this runner is a genuine unknown quantity.
runners_data.comment: An 8,000gns colt by Profitable, making his debut out of a dam who showed modest form at seven furlongs as a two-year-old; his half-brother Evelyn's Phoenix was fair at nine furlongs, and while this looks a tough opening assignment, there's pedigree substance to work with.

runners_data.name: Dreamlover
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who sits prominently and has placed once in two good-ground runs; faces the problem of two rivals with identical intent, and pressure will be on from the outset over this 6f trip.
runners_data.comment: Third in a maiden at Chester last time, beaten six and a half lengths in first-time blinkers, matched his level on debut and now drops in grade; effective at today's trip on a sound surface, and with the yard in form, he's an obvious threat here.

runners_data.name: Dream On Kent
runners_data.note: David Evans front-runner with two placed efforts at 6f on good ground suggesting genuine ability at this trip; must win the pace battle with Havana Gift and Dreamlover from the off, but if clear early could be dangerous.
runners_data.comment: A close second in a novice at Chepstow last time, wearing a visor down to six furlongs, adds to another runner-up effort in his last three starts; well suited by this trip and ground, and with the yard having landed this race twelve months ago, he holds solid claims dropping in company.

runners_data.name: Little Mester
runners_data.note: Second Stuart Williams runner with no form data whatsoever; runs alongside stablemate Champagne Charlee and represents a complete unknown — class could be anything, going suitability unverified.
runners_data.comment: A gelding by Mohaather making his racecourse debut, out of a dam who was fair form at fourteen furlongs; his half-brother Claim That Smile showed fair form at six furlongs, though this is no easy starting point at this level, leaving him with more to prove than the leading names.

runners_data.name: South West
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with two runs on good ground, both unplaced; trainer Richard Hughes sends a light-raced type who is stepping up to 6f, and the horse's profile lacks the form depth to inspire confidence despite a theoretically favourable tactical position.
runners_data.comment: A debut ninth was followed by an improved fifth at the minimum trip last time, beaten six and a quarter lengths in a maiden at this course; first-time blinkers and another drop in grade could help, but the yard's cold recent form, two winners from forty-five runners, leaves him the outsider on our figures.

runners_data.name: Tamam Star
runners_data.note: K R Burke's consistent 2-year-old with four runs on good ground including two placed efforts; prominent racing style suits a strong-pace scenario where a close-up position off the leaders can be converted in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Having underperformed in a seller at York last time, beaten nine lengths, this colt followed two thirds and a fourth and should have gone closer there; back at this trip on the sound surface he prefers, and our top-rated runner in this field, he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Turnstile
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's most battle-hardened runner with seven runs on good ground, four of them placed at 5-6f; genuine hold-up style and consistent form make it the standout pace-shape beneficiary if the front-runners tire as expected.
runners_data.comment: Third in four of his last six starts, most recently over five furlongs at Musselburgh when beaten three and a quarter lengths in a maiden, this colt races consistently around this level and is at home on a sound surface; with a big weight to carry the only obvious concern, he ranks a leading threat on our figures.

runners_data.name: Vinery
runners_data.note: David Evans hold-up type with one run at 7f on good ground, finishing sixth; stepping back to 6f on fast ground with a 5lb claiming jockey, and the limited evidence leaves its credentials here largely untested.
runners_data.comment: Sixth on his only start to date, never featuring after a slow start when beaten seven lengths in a maiden at this course, this gelding needs much more back down in trip and grade; the yard was successful in this race last year, but there's little in the form itself to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Havana Gift
runners_data.note: Front-runner with four runs on good ground, placed once, and returning quickly on just two days' rest; the tight turnaround is a concern, and facing two rivals with identical lead intentions over 6f on good-to-firm ground makes the front position costly.
runners_data.comment: A fourth in a nursery at Nottingham latest, beaten two and a quarter lengths, continues a run of competitive placed efforts, including a second two starts back; light-framed and claiming off a workable mark, she reappears quickly just two days on and is well suited by this trip on a sound surface.

runners_data.name: Yankeedoodledandy
runners_data.note: Ran last of thirteen on its sole start at 6f on good ground; the trainer's 14-day strike rate of zero and the note of fading in the finish make this a very difficult profile to recommend under any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a maiden at Windsor on her only start, hampered and never able to get competitive, this filly clearly needs a big step forward; she does have experience over today's trip and going, but on that solitary effort a major turnaround looks necessary to feature.

races.paceDynamic: Havana Gift, Dreamlover, and Dream On Kent are all confirmed front-runners, and with three horses bidding to lead over 6f at Leicester on good-to-firm ground, a strong, unrelenting early gallop is virtually certain. The three pace-setters will press each other from the stalls, burning energy through the first three furlongs and ensuring the field is strung out early, with genuine stamina demands placed on every participant by halfway. Tamam Star will look to sit prominently just off the contested lead, while hold-up horses Turnstile, South Wind, and Vinery will be given a chance to gather momentum from the rear as the pace unravels in front of them. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses with a proven hold-up or late-finishing profile who can exploit a contested lead that is likely to collapse in the final furlong — closers and stalkers who travel well within themselves will hold a clear structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out through a fast early pace and the field strings out, leaving hold-up horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: If the three front-runners burn each other out through a fast early pace and the field strings out, leaving hold-up horses to sweep through.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Sets Own Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners breaks cleanly and the others fail to match strides, allowing a single leader to control the pace at a sustainable rhythm.
scenarios.body: If one of the three front-runners breaks cleanly and the others fail to match strides, allowing a single leader to control the pace at a sustainable rhythm.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not catastrophically so, allowing a horse settled just off the early battle to cruise into contention approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is strong but not catastrophically so, allowing a horse settled just off the early battle to cruise into contention approaching the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Uninitiated Horse Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce that all pacemakers blow up entirely, creating an unusually wide-open late dash that favours unexposed runners with unknown profiles.
scenarios.body: If the pace is so fierce that all pacemakers blow up entirely, creating an unusually wide-open late dash that favours unexposed runners with unknown profiles.

watchPoints.text: Turnstile is the most exposed hold-up horse in the field with seven runs on good ground and four placed efforts — if the pace is as strong as projected, watch for David Allan to deliver it late with purpose.

Dream On Kent's ability to break cleanly and win the initial pace battle against Havana Gift and Dreamlover will be decisive — if it clears the other two front-runners in the first furlong, its 6f good-ground form makes it a live contender.

Havana Gift is returning on just two days' rest and must fight three-way for the lead — monitor any signs of laboured movement in the parade ring, as the fast turnaround combined with a contested pace role is a significant physical ask.

Champagne Charlee and Little Mester are both Stuart Williams runners with zero form lines — if either drifts significantly in the market before post time, treat it as an informational signal given the complete absence of public form data.

Tamam Star's step up from five furlongs to six on good-to-firm represents an unexplored stamina question despite consistent placed runs — watch how Jack Nicholls (5lb claim) positions it early, as getting caught in traffic in a strung-out field would be damaging.

races.name: Smooth Radio EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Anyasi
runners_data.note: OR 120 Roger Varian filly who has won over six furlongs on soft and placed on Good; a confirmed front-runner with a clear tactical advantage in this small field and the class advantage over her rivals is significant.
runners_data.comment: A clear improver from his debut effort, this colt got off the mark at Yarmouth last time, scoring by three lengths in a novice, and there should be more to come even under a penalty today; with the stable in good form and conditions on the soft side well within his compass, he's taken to follow up.

runners_data.name: Bucklow Hill
runners_data.note: Charles Hills has just one winner from 14 runners in 14 days and this gelding was last seen finishing 11th at Goodwood before winning at Catterick on Standard; he carries a tongue-tie and returns after 71 days off, making his reappearance fitness a genuine query.
runners_data.comment: A big, strong sort who could only manage a well-beaten effort down the field in a novice at Doncaster most recently, some way below the level he showed when getting off the mark previously, this colt returns off a lengthy break with a first-time tongue-tie fitted, and there's a good chance he can return to that level of form; the six-furlong trip and an all-weather surface both look right up his street.

runners_data.name: Two Commanders
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's colt finished third over seven furlongs on Good going last time and the drop to six furlongs on Good to Firm may sharpen his speed; prominent style suits him here and he maps second-best of those likely to sit close to the pace.
runners_data.comment: Showing plenty of resolve, this gelding improved on a third-placed debut to get off the mark by a narrow margin in a novice at Catterick last time over six furlongs, and there's no reason he can't follow up back at a similar trip; he's versatile on good-to-soft or good-to-firm ground and rates capable of another bold showing.

runners_data.name: Retro Rocket
runners_data.note: Martin Keighley sends out a lightly-raced three-year-old with an undefined style whose form figures of 7-10 over seven and eight furlongs on Good and Standard give little confidence over six furlongs on quick turf; the lightly-raced flag adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Two runs so far have brought little in the way of encouragement, with performances well below what's needed at this level, and there's a growing sense that a step up to middle distances is required rather than today's sprint trip; on what he's shown to date, a case for involvement here is hard to construct.

runners_data.name: Baby G
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's filly has one run to her name, an eighth over five furlongs at Lingfield on Standard, and the unknown style combined with the noted tendency to fade in the finish makes her a spectator in terms of scenario planning; seven-runner novice field gives her racing room at least.
runners_data.comment: A slow start effectively ended her chance in a maiden at Wolverhampton on her only outing, and she was never involved from there, finishing a well-beaten eighth; a significant step forward is needed on that solitary piece of form to trouble this field.

runners_data.name: Material Girl
runners_data.note: Archie Watson has been cold over 14 days with just one winner from 34 runners; she was fifth and seventh in her last two starts over six furlongs on Standard and Good going respectively and needs a bounce-back to feature here.
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held in a novice at Southwell last time, matching much the same level shown on debut, this filly looks exposed already and leaves plenty to find on what she's shown; the yard is also out of form, with just a single winner from thirty-four runners in the last fortnight, adding to the case against her at six furlongs.

runners_data.name: Red Legs
runners_data.note: Martin Dunne's hold-up performer has finished seventh and eighth on Soft and Good going over six furlongs and, as the only genuine hold-up horse in the field, faces an uphill task if the pace is controlled and there is no meaningful late acceleration to aim at.
runners_data.comment: A step forward from a poor debut still left her closer to last than midfield when beaten ten lengths in a novice at Yarmouth last time, and there remains plenty of improvement required; bred with a mile very much in mind long-term, today's six furlongs may not be doing her any favours just yet.

races.paceDynamic: Anyasi is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner novice stakes and, with no rival likely to seriously dispute her lead, she should stride into a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the outset on Good to Firm ground at Leicester. Bucklow Hill, Two Commanders, and Material Girl all carry prominent styles but none has the natural speed or profile to pressurise a horse rated OR 120 over six furlongs; the pace will therefore be honest but measured rather than searingly fast. Red Legs is the only hold-up type in the field, while Retro Rocket and Baby G are unknown quantities whose undefined styles are unlikely to disrupt the shape. This race shape strongly favours Anyasi and the prominent racers who can slot in behind her immediately, as a controlled lead on quick ground over a straight six at Leicester typically rewards those who travel in the first two or three positions rather than closers trying to make up ground from off a moderate tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Anyasi Controls, Leads Home
scenarios.trigger: If Anyasi dictates an uncontested lead and the pace remains measured throughout the six furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Anyasi dictates an uncontested lead and the pace remains measured throughout the six furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Peg Her Back
scenarios.trigger: If Two Commanders or Bucklow Hill travel strongly enough to close the gap through the final two furlongs and force a tight finish.
scenarios.body: If Two Commanders or Bucklow Hill travel strongly enough to close the gap through the final two furlongs and force a tight finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Material Girl Comes Good
scenarios.trigger: If Material Girl recovers her form for Archie Watson and the prominent racer finds a cleaner run than her recent starts suggest.
scenarios.body: If Material Girl recovers her form for Archie Watson and the prominent racer finds a cleaner run than her recent starts suggest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Sprints Through
scenarios.trigger: If Retro Rocket or Baby G, both with undefined styles, find an unexpected level of ability over the six furlongs on fast ground.
scenarios.body: If Retro Rocket or Baby G, both with undefined styles, find an unexpected level of ability over the six furlongs on fast ground.

watchPoints.text: Anyasi — watch whether she is sent straight to the front by Daniel Muscutt or if any of the prominent trio attempt to press her early, as any unexpected pressure on the lead is the key danger trigger for Scenario B.

Bucklow Hill — returning after 71 days off for Charles Hills, whose recent trainer form is poor; watch the paddock for signs of condition and whether Sean Bowen sends him forward aggressively to overcome the layoff.

Two Commanders — watch how quickly Cian Horgan positions him at the break; if the 5lb claimer gets him into a tracking position within the first furlong he becomes the most likely to give Anyasi a race in the closing stages.
Baby G and Retro Rocket — both have undefined running styles and limited form; watch where they settle in the early stages as unexpected pace from either would alter the tempo picture materially.

Material Girl — James Sullivan's positioning in the first half-furlong will reveal whether Archie Watson has asked for an aggressive prominent ride or a more conservative approach; the former is her only realistic route into the finish.

races.name: Rich And Carr Solicitors Handicap

runners_data.name: Kameel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a recent second over 10f on Good ground that reads well for this trip and surface; veteran seven-year-old form profile is consistent without being electric, but the visor is a headgear angle worth noting alongside a sharp 21-day turnaround; will need to find a gap from the back.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in six runs, Kameel ran creditably when beaten three and a quarter lengths here last time off just a pound higher, and his best form comes on synthetic. This drop back in trip should suit, with a first-time visor and a 57 rating keeping him competitive.

runners_data.name: Hachiman
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr handler with a modest T14 strike rate; all five recent runs have been over 8f and on softer or Standard ground, making this step up to 10f on Good to Firm an open stamina and going question; races from the rear and will need the pace to truly collapse for this to work.
runners_data.comment: Held up in his races, Hachiman was never involved from a slow start when beaten eight and a quarter lengths in a handicap at Doncaster last time, and he looks fully exposed since a flattering maiden success. His form claims are strongest over a mile, shorter than today's test, and with the stable out of form too, a 47 rating makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Charencey
runners_data.note: Tongue tie fitted and six-year-old experience over 10f on Good ground is present in the history, though 0W0P on similar going is not encouraging; Ian Williams has one winner from 29 runners over 14 days and this hold-up runner will need to find cover and a run from the back.
runners_data.comment: Below form of late, Charencey was beaten eight and a quarter lengths in a handicap at Chepstow last time and has yet to win in five starts, with the stable also out of form. He does have course and distance form and acts on any going, and a first-time tongue-tie could help off a 55 rating.

runners_data.name: Beryl's Girl
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; Eve Johnson Houghton in good form (T14: 4/32) and David Probert is a strong booking; won over 10f on Good ground 12 days ago, wears a hood, and faces no pace rivals — this horse's role is essentially guaranteed and the question is only whether the winning margin is comfortable or emphatic.
runners_data.comment: Beryl's Girl arrives fresh from landing a handicap by two lengths at Brighton last time, showing much needed improvement once fitted with cheekpieces up to this trip. She acts well on a sound surface and rates the one to beat on a 63 rating, though a 5lb rise means she'll have to confirm that promise.

runners_data.name: City Escape
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent type who has placed over 10f on Good going (3rd) and appreciates this trip; Nikki Evans yard is quiet (T14: 0/2) but the horse's natural racing style gives it an automatic tactical advantage in a pace-dominated scenario; ear shields fitted and has been consistent at this trip.
runners_data.comment: City Escape rates a strong threat on a 62 figure despite modest recent form, with an easing mark now working in her favour and this ten-furlong trip suiting on any going. She got over-excited and was below her best when beaten five lengths in a handicap at Bath last time, and that tendency, plus a first-time eyeshield to combat it, remains the obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Bel Air Flyer
runners_data.note: Henry Candy runner returning from a 68-day break, which is the longest absence in this field and makes fitness a genuine concern; naturally a hold-up horse who has shown a tendency to fade in the finish, and the redistribution to midfield means it will not be getting the patient ride it needs — discount accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Bel Air Flyer's best form is a fourth from three starts, with a shade more encouragement when down the field in a maiden at Lingfield last time. She may well improve now she tackles a handicap, but a 68-day absence and a 50 rating leave a fair bit to find.

runners_data.name: Argentum
runners_data.note: Steps back down significantly in trip from recent outings over 14f and 16f, which raises real questions about whether 10f is now genuinely sharp enough; Ryan Kavanagh claims 5lb and Matt Crawley has 0 winners from 4 runs over 14 days — mapped to midfield but a true hold-up type, making a winning position hard to secure.
runners_data.comment: Argentum had nothing more to give at an unsuitable fourteen furlongs when well beaten in a handicap at Yarmouth last time, and she's still without a win in six starts. Today's ten furlongs is shorter than her best form around eleven to twelve, and although she acts on a sound surface, a 51 rating makes her tough to support.

runners_data.name: A Daughters Love
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good ground and placed in two others at the same trip, so the form profile is the most directly relevant in the field; David Flood has a quiet book (T14: 0/7) and only ran 7 days ago, but this three-year-old's genuine desire to race positively means the midfield map position may actually undersell how close to the pace it ends up.
runners_data.comment: A Daughters Love struck for the first time when landing a handicap by three and a quarter lengths at Chepstow last time, just seven days ago, and there should be more to come now she has that success under her belt. She stays this ten-furlong trip well on a sound surface and rates a serious threat on a 62 figure, though she does have to defy a 6lb rise.

runners_data.name: Arc At Her
runners_data.note: Three-run career entirely over 8f, meaning this 10f outing is an untested stamina trip; Dylan Cunha is showing some form (T14: 2/29) but this filly has finished 9th on Good going previously and fading in the finish is a noted tendency — the combination of trip doubt and style penalty make this one of the harder cases to back.
runners_data.comment: A recent import from Ireland, Arc At Her looks sure to improve for a switch to handicaps, with her only sign of encouragement coming when down the field in a maiden at Lingfield last time after racing off the pace. She's rated a leading contender on 59, but her form to date is all on synthetic over nine furlongs, leaving today's ground and the step up in trip both unproven.

runners_data.name: Diamond Aura
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer in reasonable form (T14: 4/51) and Sean Bowen is a high-quality jockey booking that stands out; has run well on Good ground over 10f (4th last time) and the step up from 8f to 10f appears to suit, though as a true hold-up type placed in midfield, Bowen will need to thread through — the jockey quality gives this one a small edge in traffic.
runners_data.comment: Diamond Aura ran to expectation when beaten four lengths off a 2lb higher mark at Brighton last time, and with the stable currently among the winners, she has a squeak if she builds on that. She's without a win in five starts and toils near the foot of the weights on a 53 rating, but she does act well on a sound surface over this trip.

races.paceDynamic: Beryl's Girl is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m2f handicap on Good to Firm ground at Leicester, and with no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, she can dictate a comfortable, controlled gallop from the front. City Escape holds a prominent position from her draw and may track close behind, but neither she nor any other runner has the profile or inclination to press Beryl's Girl into a genuinely hot tempo. With one pacesetter setting a sustainable rhythm on fast ground over a middle-distance trip, the race shape strongly favours horses who can sit handy and accelerate into the straight — hold-up horses will need to find ground and momentum that a slow-to-moderate pace may not generate. This field holds significantly more hold-up types than can realistically operate from their natural rear position; Beryl's Girl and City Escape are best placed to secure their roles, while Kameel, Charencey, Hachiman, A Daughters Love, Arc At Her, Bel Air Flyer, Argentum, and Diamond Aura are all broadly hold-up or midfield types competing for the same late ground — the horses most capable of racing closer to the pace, such as A Daughters Love (recent good-ground winner) and Diamond Aura, have the best chance of travelling within striking range.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beryl's Girl Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Beryl's Girl is allowed to stride clear at a comfortable clip and the field fails to close the gap entering the straight.
scenarios.body: If Beryl's Girl is allowed to stride clear at a comfortable clip and the field fails to close the gap entering the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pull Clear
scenarios.trigger: If City Escape or a hold-up horse manages to travel just off the pace and the gap to the pack becomes decisive from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: If City Escape or a hold-up horse manages to travel just off the pace and the gap to the pack becomes decisive from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely too strong and Beryl's Girl ties up in the final furlong, opening the door for the midfield pack.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is genuinely too strong and Beryl's Girl ties up in the final furlong, opening the door for the midfield pack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Lands Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops chaotically with the midfield group bunching and an unfancied runner threads through late in fortunate circumstances.
scenarios.body: If the race develops chaotically with the midfield group bunching and an unfancied runner threads through late in fortunate circumstances.

watchPoints.text: Beryl's Girl — if David Probert allows her to stride clear early without being pressed, the controlled pace she sets could render the entire hold-up group irrelevant, as they will lack the strong gallop needed to close from the rear on fast ground.

City Escape — watch whether Kieran O'Neill pushes up to track Beryl's Girl closely in the first half-mile; if City Escape secures second spot, it gives the nine-year-old a major tactical advantage and becomes the biggest threat to the leader in the straight.

A Daughters Love — despite being mapped to midfield, this three-year-old has won and placed three times over this exact trip on Good ground; if Jack Doughty gets a prominent position closer to the pace than the map suggests, this runner's form profile makes it a genuine threat.

Bel Air Flyer — the 68-day absence combined with a tendency to fade late and the style penalty from redistribution makes this one of the horses most at risk of running below expectations; monitor market moves but treat any support with caution.

Diamond Aura — Sean Bowen's booking on a Palmer-trained horse stepping up to a more suitable trip on ideal ground is a combination worth tracking in the market; any significant downward move in price would suggest stable confidence.

races.name: Curve Theatre Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Lodge
runners_data.note: Has one win from five on similar going and a recent course win on good ground, but has been absent 82 days and drops from 7f on Tapeta to 6f on turf — the natural hold-up style means she needs the pace to be genuinely strong and sustained to mount a challenge from the rear.
runners_data.comment: The form has gone in the wrong direction since a debut win, with this filly well beaten last time here having raced too freely and used up her energy too soon in a handicap; she returns for the first time in almost three months with a first-time tongue-tie fitted, and while she does act on this sort of ground, the leading form clearly poses a stern task.

runners_data.name: Dolo's Star
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride for Grant Tuer whose stable is in decent form (3/9 last 14 days), but all three career starts have been over 5f on Tapeta — the step up to 6f on turf is an unknown, and hold-up racing style offers limited confidence at a trip where she has no proven form.
runners_data.comment: A big-priced second in a novice at Southwell latest, beaten three quarters of a length, may have run above her true level that day, and there's a question over whether she can repeat it now stepping up to six furlongs on turf having previously been proven at the minimum trip on synthetic surfaces; she returns quickly after that break and sits bottom of this field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Carefree Dream
runners_data.note: Donagh Murphy (7lb claim) partners this consistent 3yo for J S Moore who has 0 wins from 19 runners in 14 days — she has placed at 5f on good and soft but moves to 6f today with a natural hold-up style that must wait for the pace to do the work ahead of her.
runners_data.comment: Keen but game in defeat when beaten just a length off a slightly lower mark at Goodwood last time, this filly ran to form there and has been runner-up in each of her last two starts; she's clearly in good order right now and, with the figures suggesting she's effective down to five furlongs on any going, she's a leading player again off this mark.

runners_data.name: Guernsey Angel
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave is an experienced pilot for David Evans, who is in fair form (3/24), and Guernsey Angel's prominent style suits the likely race shape — however she has run six consecutive races without a win or place and her five-run losing streak at 5-6f flags a form concern.
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held back up at six furlongs in a handicap at Haydock last time, this filly didn't see out the trip fully there, continuing a run of modest finishes without ever threatening; she does act well on quick ground or all-weather, but more is clearly needed to get involved in this company.

runners_data.name: Sayidah Aleen
runners_data.note: Front-runner with hood/pads (hg:p) dropped back from 7-8f trips by Marco Botti, suggesting a speed-first tactic — she will battle May Encounter for the lead and if she can settle on the front and quicken, the trip could suit, though her best form came at longer distances.
runners_data.comment: Not seeing out a step up to a mile on soft ground when a close third at Lingfield most recently, this filly has otherwise gone well in maiden company, placing once more before that; back closer to her best trip with first-time cheekpieces added, she can't be ruled out on her first attempt at a handicap.

runners_data.name: Q T Pie
runners_data.note: William Carson partners this Tom Dascombe 3yo who has a win and two places in five runs, including a 6f good-ground win in her form string — a naturally prominent racer on a going she handles, with a trainer showing 3/14 in 14 days, she fits the dominant scenario shape well.
runners_data.comment: A revival of form saw her beaten just half a length off a lighter mark at Goodwood last time, and that comeback run, her first of the season, should bring improvement with a race under her belt; effective at today's trip on this sort of ground as a two-year-old, she rates a leading contender again.

runners_data.name: Amelia's Joy
runners_data.note: Michael Herrington's 4yo has a strong record in similar going (3 places from 15 sim-going runs) and David Probert takes the ride — prominent style suits a race with genuine front-running pace ahead of her, though she has been running over 7f and steps back to 6f today.
runners_data.comment: Splitting two wins either side of a handful of minor-place finishes, this filly continues to race to a fair level, and was beaten just half a length last time off a mark of sixty-two, only a pound lower than today; the yard is in good form, first-time cheekpieces are added, and she looks competitive again at a trip she handles well.

runners_data.name: Sierra Sue
runners_data.note: James Horton (0/6 in 14 days) sends out this lightly-weighted 3yo who is a genuine hold-up type by nature, though the crowded rear means she has been mapped to midfield — her form at 6f on good ground (5th and 4th) is modest and the style compromise tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Beaten eight and a quarter lengths in a handicap at Redcar last time but running to her level there, this filly has a workable, easing mark in her favour today, and first-time cheekpieces could sharpen her up further; she's suited by this trip on quick or soft ground, giving her a fair chance if she can find more.

runners_data.name: May Encounter
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's 4yo has contested every race over 6f with front-running intent and will battle Sayidah Aleen for the early lead — her recent form shows five consecutive 4th-6th finishes without a win or place, suggesting she serves the pace but lacks the finishing kick to convert.
runners_data.comment: A modest effort at Nottingham last time, beaten three lengths from a mark two pounds higher than today, leaves this filly something of an unknown quantity on recent evidence, having failed to add to a run of similar finishing positions beforehand; she should be suited by this trip on a sound surface, but the case for her remains unclear.

runners_data.name: Spacewoman
runners_data.note: Recent 6f good-ground winner (1/6f/GOO) for Henry Candy who also trains May Encounter, giving the yard tactical options — she is a natural hold-up type by profile but with more closers than the map accommodates, she may not find her ideal position, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 is a mild caution.
runners_data.comment: A neck victory down to six furlongs at Newmarket last time, off a mark four pounds lower than today, marked this filly's first success and came after finding herself suited by a drop in trip; she looks open to further progress still as an out-and-out sprinter, remains unexposed at the trip, and heads this field on our figures despite stamina beyond six furlongs still unproven.

runners_data.name: Grand Citadel
runners_data.note: Grace McEntee rides this 5yo for Micky Fenton who has only 1 runner in 14 days — has an excellent record on good ground (1W 4P from 15 sim-going runs) and recent 6f course form, making prominent style over this trip on good-to-firm a genuine fit if she travels well early.
runners_data.comment: A well-held tenth back down to six furlongs last time, beaten ten lengths off the same mark she races off today, was a big step back for this mare after an earlier spell of form that had brought a win among some encouraging placed efforts; first-time blinkers are added in the hope of a return to form, and she does act across a wide range of trips and going.

races.paceDynamic: Sayidah Aleen and May Encounter are the two confirmed front-runners in this 11-runner 6f fillies' handicap on good-to-firm Leicester turf, and with both likely to push for the lead from the gates, this race will be run at an honest, competitive gallop rather than a crawl. Sayidah Aleen's hg:p tag and recent form over 7-8f suggests she is being dropped back for speed, while May Encounter has consistent 6f form and the Henry Candy yard knows the trip — expect a genuine two-way tussle for the early lead that will sustain the tempo throughout. The contested pace sets this up as a race where prominent racers who can travel just off the duelling leaders and produce a clean, well-timed run into the straight will be best placed, rather than pure front-runners who burn energy in the battle or deep closers who have too much ground to make up. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Sierra Sue and Spacewoman are genuine hold-up horses pushed into midfield representation, meaning Q T Pie, Amelia's Joy, and Guernsey Angel are most likely to physically secure the prominent positions they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sayidah Aleen and May Encounter fight for the lead and sustain a strong gallop, setting up the race perfectly for a prominent racer travelling just behind.
scenarios.body: If Sayidah Aleen and May Encounter fight for the lead and sustain a strong gallop, setting up the race perfectly for a prominent racer travelling just behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace setters — most likely Sayidah Aleen — breaks smartly and May Encounter concedes the lead early, allowing a solo front-runner to control fractions.
scenarios.body: If one of the two pace setters — most likely Sayidah Aleen — breaks smartly and May Encounter concedes the lead early, allowing a solo front-runner to control fractions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the contested lead produces a truly hot pace and the field strings out early, creating a sprint-home finale for the back markers.
scenarios.body: If the contested lead produces a truly hot pace and the field strings out early, creating a sprint-home finale for the back markers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Comes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate despite the two front-runners and the field bunches, producing a messy, scrimmaging finish where a midfielder threads through.
scenarios.body: If the pace is moderate despite the two front-runners and the field bunches, producing a messy, scrimmaging finish where a midfielder threads through.

watchPoints.text: Sayidah Aleen and May Encounter will clash for the lead from the gates — watch the first furlong to see which one concedes; if May Encounter lets Sayidah Aleen through cleanly, the solo front-runner scenario becomes live immediately.

Q T Pie showed a 6f good-ground win earlier in her form string and William Carson rides prominently — if she settles just behind the duelling leaders in second or third, she is the most dangerous horse in the dominant scenario and worth tracking from halfway.

Grand Citadel's record of 1W 4P from 15 runs on similar going is the best in the field — Grace McEntee will need to find a prominent position early given the competitive pace, and any trouble in running in the first two furlongs would significantly harm her chance.

Lodge has been off 82 days and switches from Tapeta 7f to turf 6f — Finley Marsh will need to produce a confident, well-timed hold-up run, but the going and distance change combined with the layoff means she needs everything to fall right late in the race.

Spacewoman and Sierra Sue are both genuine hold-up types who cannot both race from their natural position — watch the early stages to see if either gets shuffled wider or forward against her style, as a horse racing in an unnatural position is a structural risk in a race that will be run at pace.

races.name: KLG Rutland Handicap

runners_data.name: Mr Writer
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 7f on Good going and is the confirmed pace-setter here — Daniel Muscutt rides for the in-form James Fanshawe stable (7 winners from 28 in 14 days) and the 15-day turnaround is ideal, but Mr Writer's role is to set the race up rather than win it at OR 78.
runners_data.comment: Fifth when not staying a mile at Goodwood last time, he still ran to his mark for much of it, and a drop back to seven furlongs suits after a win and two places in his last five starts; he carries top weight but with the yard in form, he rates the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Galileo Island
runners_data.note: Marco Botti fires just 1 from 12 in the past fortnight but Galileo Island's form profile is the strongest in the field for this trip and going — winning at 7f on Good ground and placing three more times in similar conditions makes this the horse most naturally suited by an uncontested pace.
runners_data.comment: A below-form eighth at Doncaster last time reflected a stamina issue in a competitive handicap rather than a loss of ability, following a solid recent sequence that included a win and two further places; first-time cheekpieces and a return to seven furlongs, a trip he handles well, should help turn that form around.

runners_data.name: Cashbox
runners_data.note: Charles Hills sends this one out on a 21-day break following a disappointing 7th last time out, but the two prior wins on Good-to-Firm/Standard ground over this exact trip are the key credentials — David Probert is a sharp tactical jockey who will ensure Cashbox is positioned to pounce if the pace stays controlled.
runners_data.comment: Below-par again when beaten five lengths in a handicap at Sandown last time, this is now two runs without a repeat of the form that brought a pair of wins, and a return to form is overdue; cheekpieces go on for the first time and he does act well at this trip on a sound surface, but our figures rate him one of the more vulnerable in this field.

runners_data.name: Loquella
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston has 4 winners from 37 runners over 14 days and Loquella arrives after a 64-day break, which is the longest layoff in this field — the horse's natural hold-up style suits a scenario where the pace is honest enough to generate a closing run, though Sean Bowen will need to find clear daylight early in the straight.
runners_data.comment: A fifth in a handicap at Newcastle last time, below the level she showed in novice company and beaten five lengths, arrives over two months since that run; she's normally suited by a sharper six furlongs than today's test, though she does act on this surface, and with more needed on the balance of that form, she's up against it in this line-up.

runners_data.name: Pints In Peace
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's runner has placed twice at 7f on Standard but has no wins or places on similar Going here (0W0P in five runs on Good or similar), making the going suitability the primary concern — a natural hold-up type who needs a genuinely run race and free passage to be competitive from OR 72.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten seventh last time from a higher mark of 77, some way below his level on that occasion, this gelding still holds a pair of wins in his last six starts and races off a more workable 72 today; a first-time tongue-tie could aid focus, and he handles quick and soft ground alike, though there's a little more to prove back on turf.

runners_data.name: Frantic
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's runner has two placed efforts at 6f on Good ground and is a true prominent racer by profile, but the field is too stacked with front-runners for Frantic to secure that position naturally, pushing Ashley Lewis into the difficult task of settling mid-division; the 5lb claim helps the weight but the positional compromise materially dents the chance.
runners_data.comment: A luckless seventh last time, only beaten three lengths off her current mark despite not enjoying the run of the race, arrives on the back of three runner-up finishes and a fourth in her other recent starts; well suited by this trip on any surface, she rates a fair chance again among the principals.

runners_data.name: Eduardo Calderon
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's gelding has placed twice at 7f on Good ground (2nd most recently) and arrives after 44 days off, with his natural running style being hold-up — squeezed into a midfield map position here because the hold-up section of this field is already occupied, meaning Kaiya Fraser faces a tactical puzzle from the lowest OR in the race.
runners_data.comment: A fourth in a handicap at Haydock last time, beaten six lengths and true to his level there, sits on the back of a mixed campaign that includes a runner-up effort among the placings; a six-week absence hasn't dimmed the promise of more to offer under handicap conditions, and he's effective at this trip on quick and soft ground alike.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Writer is the confirmed front runner on this card and will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the off — with no genuine rival willing to take him on for the lead, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching on Good to Firm ground over seven furlongs at Leicester. Galileo Island, Cashbox, and the redistributed Frantic are all naturally prominent types, but only two can realistically sit close behind Mr Writer, meaning at least one of those three will be squeezed into a position further back than ideal. This field holds more prominent-profile horses than the race shape can accommodate at the front, with Galileo Island and Cashbox — both with superior form credentials at this trip and going — best placed to secure the early rail positions behind the pace-setter. A steady-to-moderate gallop set by Mr Writer with two prominent horses tracking closely is a shape that strongly favours confirmed hold-up closers with a potent late kick, but given Loquella and Eduardo Calderon are the only true hold-up types, the race is most likely to reward the horse who sits closest to the even pace and picks off the leader in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Writer sets a steady, uncontested pace and Galileo Island and Cashbox settle directly behind him, their momentum into the straight proves decisive.
scenarios.body: If Mr Writer sets a steady, uncontested pace and Galileo Island and Cashbox settle directly behind him, their momentum into the straight proves decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and a significant gap opens between the front group and the closers by halfway, creating enough run to get home late.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely moderate and a significant gap opens between the front group and the closers by halfway, creating enough run to get home late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Frantic Grabs Rail
scenarios.trigger: If Frantic uses early speed to assert against expectations and forces a contested pace that stretches the field from the front.
scenarios.body: If Frantic uses early speed to assert against expectations and forces a contested pace that stretches the field from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent types overwork each other in a compressed mid-race bunch and Eduardo Calderon produces an uncharacteristic well-timed late challenge.
scenarios.body: If the prominent types overwork each other in a compressed mid-race bunch and Eduardo Calderon produces an uncharacteristic well-timed late challenge.

watchPoints.text: Mr Writer has the pace stolen — if Frantic's jockey pushes forward aggressively from stall draw, it forces a contested pace that could detonate the entire prominent group turning for home.

Galileo Island's trainer Marco Botti is out of form at 1/12 over the past fortnight — watch for any market drift in the final hour that might signal the team is not confident despite the strong form profile.

Loquella's 64-day absence is the longest layoff in this field — Charlie Johnston horses can need a run after a break of this length, and Sean Bowen will need the horse to be cherry-ripe on reappearance to justify the wait.

Cashbox was beaten 13 lengths last time out on Good ground over this exact trip — if that run is ignored and market confidence builds, it is worth monitoring whether the trainer has applied any equipment change or different race tactics via Probert's positioning at the break.

Eduardo Calderon's most recent win was on Soft ground, and all five sampled runs on Good or similar have produced zero wins and zero places — the going suitability is a factual concern worth noting before the off.

races.name: Appliance City Bunny 'Confined' Handicap

runners_data.name: Palmarian
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for Ruth Carr but likely to occupy a midfield berth here; 15 days since last run is a positive freshness angle, yet their sim-going record of five wins from 12 on similar ground without a win is a concern over this mile trip.
runners_data.comment: Palmarian ran up to his level when beaten nine lengths in a handicap at Redcar last time, undone by racing too freely again, and he remains without a win in six starts. He has course and distance form in the book, but stretching out beyond his sharper seven-furlong form is a query, and with a first-time hood, a stable out of form, and a 60 rating, he's hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: My Ambition
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley's seven-year-old has strong form at this trip on faster surfaces (1W1P from six similar-going runs) but has been off 53 days and, as a genuine rear-of-field type, will be racing ahead of where they want to be in what is essentially a one-pace-setter race.
runners_data.comment: My Ambition showed solid form when runner-up and third in two of his last three starts, before an underwhelming effort when beaten nine lengths in a handicap at Bath last time, undone by racing too freely. Back after 53 days, he gets his conditions over this mile on a sound surface and rates a major player on 74, though there's a risk he takes too strong a hold again if he fails to settle.

runners_data.name: Aspire To Glory
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field and a key tactical linchpin; recent form reads poorly (0-0-0 in last three) but a hat-trick of STA-surface efforts may understate ability on today's good-to-firm; Ashley Lewis (5) riding, and trainer Dylan Cunha has one winner from 17 runs over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Aspire To Glory has little to recommend him on recent evidence, having been below form again when down the field in a handicap at Wolverhampton latest, and he's managed only one win in his last five starts. He does act well on an easy surface or the all-weather over today's trip, but back after a break of 54 days and up against sharper types, a 60 rating looks about right.

runners_data.name: Little Ted
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's nine-year-old arrives on just nine days' rest — the freshest horse in the field — and has placed twice at the mile trip on good ground; hood-wearing veteran who, though a natural hold-up type, has enough tactical speed to sit closer to the pace than their style label suggests.
runners_data.comment: Little Ted heads the market on our figures, having gone down by only a head at Newcastle last time from a mark 2lb lower than today's. He's proven at this trip and on sound ground, and building on that narrow defeat, a rating of 79 makes him the one to beat, with a want of a win in six starts his only real query.

runners_data.name: Aurelune
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with all recent form on soft or standard ground, which makes good-to-firm conditions a query; Richard & Fahey have eight winners from 55 over 14 days, suggesting the yard is live, but the step to firmer going for a horse rated 59 on this seasonal debut at the trip is a risk.
runners_data.comment: Aurelune managed little up at ten furlongs when well beaten in a handicap at Nottingham last time, and she remains without a win in four starts. Back to a trip within her best 7-9f range and on a sound surface, she has conditions in her favour, but a 60 rating and a wide draw leave her work cut out.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Bright
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston three-year-old who has placed three times in last five including a third on standard ground at the mile; 30 days off is acceptable and sim-going shows three places from ten attempts, suggesting the horse handles this sort of surface — a prominent ride from Daniel Muscutt suits this race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Sovereign Bright rates a big player back down to a mile having raced too freely up at ten furlongs when beaten nine lengths in a handicap at Wetherby last time. First-time cheekpieces could help settle her, and she goes well on quicker ground or the all-weather, giving her claims on a rating of 76, though she needs to find better than that below-par effort.

runners_data.name: Avispado
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's lightly-raced three-year-old has only one comparable going run in their history and is being asked to race closer to the pace than their natural instinct; the 21-day break is fine but the style-fit concern (0.90) combined with limited evidence on good-to-firm makes them speculative.
runners_data.comment: Avispado did have his excuses when fourth, beaten eight lengths in a handicap at this course last time, with the form working out better than the bare result suggests. He remains without a win in four starts and sits bottom of the field on a 58 rating, but conditions over today's trip suit and the yard is in good form, while a wide draw is a complication.

runners_data.name: Stole My Heart
runners_data.note: David Evans runner who has been placed just once from five runs on comparable going and whose form string (66-883) shows no recent upswing; a natural hold-up type forced into a midfield role, their chance is dampened by both the race shape and a modest sim-going strike rate.
runners_data.comment: Stole My Heart ran up to expectations when third, beaten seven and a quarter lengths in a handicap at Wolverhampton last time, despite showing signs it wasn't straightforward. She's a fair yardstick for this level on her day and rates a threat on 67, though stepping up beyond her sharper 6-7f form and a lack of a win in five starts leave a question mark.

runners_data.name: Leia Antilles
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's filly has the lowest weight in the race (120lbs) and Sean Bowen takes the ride, but four runs on good ground have yielded four mid-field finishes and the style-fit flag (0.90) reflects that she will not be racing from her preferred deep position today.
runners_data.comment: Leia Antilles showed better form down at this mile trip when cheekpieces were fitted last time, finishing fourth, beaten seven lengths, in a handicap at Bath. She's suited by good ground over today's distance and has a squeak if she builds further, but she remains without a win in five starts and is up against sharper types on 62.

races.paceDynamic: Aspire To Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner mile handicap and, with no other genuine pace-pusher likely to challenge them for the lead, they are set to control proceedings at a sustainable, uncontested tempo on good-to-firm ground at Leicester. That lone-leader scenario typically produces a falsely steady early pace that compresses the field and can make it difficult for true hold-up horses to generate the momentum needed to reel in a fresher front-runner in the straight. The rest of the field — My Ambition, Avispado, Stole My Heart, Little Ted, and Leia Antilles — are all natural hold-up types who are likely to be pushed into midfield roles simply because the map has no room for them all at the rear, meaning their redistribution reduces the quality of any late finishing surge. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and pounce in the final two furlongs, rather than those needing a strong gallop to be set up for a closing run from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Aspire Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Aspire To Glory jumps well, sets a controlled solo lead, and the field fails to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Aspire To Glory jumps well, sets a controlled solo lead, and the field fails to close the gap in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominently-tracking horse sits a length or two off Aspire To Glory and quickens past them entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If a prominently-tracking horse sits a length or two off Aspire To Glory and quickens past them entering the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough — or collapses — to compress the field and open a gap for a finisher coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the pace is strong enough — or collapses — to compress the field and open a gap for a finisher coming from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Capitulates
scenarios.trigger: If Aspire To Glory sets too hot a pace unsustainably and fades, gifting the race to a chasing pack.
scenarios.body: If Aspire To Glory sets too hot a pace unsustainably and fades, gifting the race to a chasing pack.

watchPoints.text: Aspire To Glory's early jump and lead establishment is the single most important moment of the race — if they miss the break or are challenged immediately, the entire pace map collapses and the race becomes genuinely open.

Sovereign Bright tracking Aspire To Glory from second or third position is the most dangerous shape in the race; watch whether Daniel Muscutt positions them right on the heels of the leader from the outset, as that would be a significant betting signal.

Little Ted's nine-day turnaround under Tim Easterby — a trainer who fires horses back quickly when ready — may mean this veteran is sharper than their recent form suggests; watch market moves as post time approaches.

The going is listed as Good To Firm for this race despite the header referencing Good — confirm at the course because any drying since early races could sharpen the surface further and tighten the advantage for prominent horses who race handily.

My Ambition's 53-day absence and genuine hold-up style mean they need an unusually strong pace to deliver their best; if they are seen tracking more prominently than usual in the first quarter-mile, it is a sign George Bass is adapting to the race shape rather than riding to form.

races.name: Bunches Handicap

runners_data.name: Moonhall Lass
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who has won twice over six and seven furlongs on good ground and arrives here nine days after a win, giving her strong course and going profile; visor fitted, which keeps her sharp, and Muscutt is an experienced claimer who will place her late — the question is whether the compressed chase pack can reel in an unhurried Rianka.
runners_data.comment: Moonhall Lass arrives in tremendous form, striking last time when landing a handicap by two and a quarter lengths here fitted with a visor, backed up by three wins from her last six starts overall. She goes on quick ground over this trip and rates a big threat on 67, though she does have to defy a 4lb rise having claimed that prize from an easier mark.

runners_data.name: Elvetham
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has placed in four of her last five over six furlongs on good ground and makes her move from just behind the leader; the 0/8 trainer 14-day strike rate is unremarkable but Conrad Allen's horses are often well-prepared, and a clean trip in second is exactly the position she naturally wants — she needs Rianka to tire.
runners_data.comment: Elvetham has a win and three thirds among his last six starts, but he needs to put a well-beaten twelfth last time behind him, easier now by a pound. Effective at this trip, and with conditions no worries on any ground, first-time blinkers could be the key to rediscovering better form, and he still rates a threat on 60.

runners_data.name: Due Date
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural place is at the back, shown in midfield on the map only because the field's hold-up population exceeds the available rear slots — his last five runs are all STA ground and he has not broken the front-six since; the extended layoff of 59 days adds a fitness question on top of a style mismatch with this race shape, and his chance must be tempered accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Due Date has struggled to be competitive in six starts without a win, running to form when beaten four lengths off a 2lb higher mark at Kempton last time. He does drop in the weights today and gets his ideal conditions over this sprint trip on a sound surface, but a lengthy 59-day gap and a first-time visor add to the uncertainty on a modest 49 rating.

runners_data.name: Melissa Honey
runners_data.note: Has won and placed multiple times on good ground over six furlongs and arrives here 13 days after a placed effort, showing solid recent form; by nature a hold-up horse placed into a midfield map slot due to the density of closers in this field, which means she may not get the clear run she needs — Probert will need a seam to open in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Melissa Honey confirmed her improvement when a close second, beaten only half a length, last time out, backing up a win from two starts back, and she remains on a workable mark for another bold bid. She's suited by this trip on quick ground or the all-weather, the stable is in form, and she rates a big threat on 67 up just a pound.

runners_data.name: Great Success
runners_data.note: Five-day turnaround for the Fahey yard who run large numbers and keep their horses fit; a hold-up horse who has finished fourth twice on good ground over six furlongs but shows no win from five tries in similar conditions, and the 0/1 placed-from-1 sim-going record is thin — talented enough to appear but needs more from this race shape than it naturally offers.
runners_data.comment: Great Success was below his best when beaten three lengths off this same mark at Pontefract last time, faltering without response in the closing stages, and he remains without a win in five starts. He is suited by this trip on fast ground or synthetic, though he needs to reverse that form quickly on a five-day turnaround to make an impact on 60.

runners_data.name: Bridget's Baby
runners_data.note: Won at five furlongs and placed at five furlongs on good ground, so the step to six is worth noting as a potential stamina query; a true hold-up type whose map position is midfield only by redistribution, and while the claimer's seven-pound allowance helps on the weights, racing off a wide-open field scenario is her best chance — standard race shapes leave her chasing too much ground.
runners_data.comment: Bridget's Baby heads the market having broken her duck readily, landing a handicap by two lengths at Lingfield last time with distance to spare. A 5lb rise is the obvious query, but she's proven at today's course, distance and going, and rates the one to beat on 69 as she continues to progress.

runners_data.name: Rianka
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and therefore the pivotal horse; has not won in four starts but her going is good-to-firm, she wears a tongue-tie, and she is completely unchallenged for the lead here — the sole question is whether her OR of 52 reflects enough raw ability to sustain the lead once the hold-up horses start closing in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Rianka failed to settle and lacked the pace to finish her race when beaten five and a half lengths in a handicap at Windsor last time, and she remains without a win in four starts. A first-time tongue-tie could help settle her, and the step up to this six-furlong trip on quicker ground looks a definite plus, but a 47 rating leaves her with plenty to find.

races.paceDynamic: Rianka is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival willing or able to press her hard from the gates, she should stride into an uncontested lead and control every fraction on this good-to-firm Leicester six furlongs. Behind her, Elvetham is the only genuine prominent-type in the field and will track Rianka in second, meaning the pace is set by one horse with a single cover horse rather than any meaningful pressure from behind. The bulk of the field — Moonhall Lass, Due Date, Melissa Honey, Bridget's Baby, and Great Success — are all hold-up types by nature, with Due Date, Melissa Honey, and Bridget's Baby redistributed to midfield on the map only because there are more true closers than the rear slots can accommodate; in reality this race will be strung out with a compact hold-up group hunting a potentially untroubled front-runner. On good-to-firm ground over six furlongs at Leicester, where a sustainable lead allows a front-runner to conserve energy and sprint clear, this race shape strongly favours Rianka if she can control the tempo, with the primary danger coming from any hold-up horse with a sharp enough turn of foot to close the gap in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Rianka's break from the stalls is critical — if she misses the kick, there is no other confirmed lead horse to set the shape and the entire race dynamic collapses into a messy, unstructured contest that could flatter any runner.

Moonhall Lass arrives on a nine-day turnaround after a win and is the most dangerous hold-up horse in the field — watch where Muscutt positions her at the two-furlong pole; if she has daylight, she will finish fastest of the closers.

Due Date has not run in 59 days, has five consecutive starts on Stanway ground, and is a genuine hold-up type placed out of natural role here — monitor whether he is visibly struggling for position in the early stages, which would confirm a non-threatening run.

Elvetham's proximity to Rianka throughout will be the key visual cue — if she is tight on Rianka's quarters entering the straight with Wood sitting still, Rianka's winning chance shortens markedly and Elvetham's win probability rises.

Bridget's Baby is ridden by a 7lb claimer (Myla Coppins) who reduces her weight to 127lbs — watch the draw and early positioning; if the claim allows her to track closer than her natural style suggests, she could be more involved than her redistribution tag implies.
